examples.ko: 교통 법규 위반자는 벌금을 내야 해요.
examples.en: Traffic law violators have to pay a fine.
The police are looking for the rule violator.
A notice is stuck on the car of the parking violator.
I heard they stepped up enforcement because violators kept increasing.
The list of violators was posted online.

examples.ko: 마스크 규정 위반자는 입장할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Those who violate the mask rule cannot enter.

explain: 주로 법, 규칙, 규정을 어긴 사람을 가리킬 때 써요. '교통 법규 위반자'처럼 앞에 어긴 내용을 붙이는 경우가 많고, 뉴스나 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '규칙을 어긴 사람'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for a person who broke a law, rule or regulation. It often comes with what was broken, like '교통 법규 위반자', and you see it in news and notices. In daily talk people also say '규칙을 어긴 사람'.

examples.en: People work wearing sanitary uniforms in a food factory.
I sweat a lot inside the sanitary uniform.
I change into a sanitary uniform before entering the kitchen.
The new sanitary uniforms haven't arrived yet.
The sanitary uniform comes with a hat and mask too.

examples.ko: 이 위생복은 하루에 한 번 세탁해요.
examples.en: This sanitary uniform is washed once a day.

explain: 음식을 다루는 곳이나 병원, 공장처럼 깨끗해야 하는 곳에서 입는 옷이에요. 보통 '위생복을 입다/갈아입다'로 말해요. 의사가 입는 '가운'이나 일반 '작업복'과는 쓰는 장소와 목적이 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It is clothing worn in places that must stay clean, such as food kitchens, hospitals and factories. It is usually used as '위생복을 입다/갈아입다'. It differs from a doctor's '가운' or ordinary '작업복' in where and why it is worn.

examples.en: What that person says is so hypocritical.
A hypocritical attitude shows quickly.
Her pretending to be kind felt hypocritical.
I dislike hypocritical people the most.
I think smiling only on the outside is hypocritical.
The reporter pointed out the politician's hypocritical remark.

explain: '-적'이 붙은 말이라 '위선적인 사람'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미거나 '위선적이에요'처럼 써요. 겉과 속이 다른 행동을 비판하는 말이라 다소 강하게 들리니, 직접 사람에게 말할 때는 조심하세요. 비슷한 말로 '가식적'이 있어요.
explain_en: Because it ends in '-적', it is used like '위선적인 사람' to modify a noun or like '위선적이에요'. It criticizes people whose outside and inside differ, so it sounds strong; be careful saying it to someone directly. A similar word is '가식적'.

examples.en: I read a lot of biographies of great figures as a child.
The biography of Admiral Yi Sun-sin was the most fun.
I chose a biography of a great figure for my child at the bookstore.

examples.ko: 위인전 속 이야기를 보고 꿈이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I got a dream after reading the stories in a biography.
The children's corner of the library is full of biographies.

examples.ko: 이 위인전은 그림이 많아서 읽기 쉬워요.
examples.en: This biography has lots of pictures, so it is easy to read.

explain: 주로 어린이용으로 만든 훌륭한 사람의 일생 책을 말해요. 일반적인 '전기'나 '자서전'보다 어릴 때 읽는 책이라는 느낌이 강해요. '위인전을 읽다'로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to books for children about the lives of admirable people. Compared with '전기' or '자서전', it strongly suggests a book you read when young. It is commonly used as '위인전을 읽다'.

examples.ko: 저는 위장병 때문에 매운 음식을 못 먹어요.
examples.en: I can't eat spicy food because of my stomach trouble.
My father has suffered from a stomach disorder for a long time.

examples.ko: 스트레스가 심하면 위장병이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Heavy stress can cause stomach trouble.
Regular meals are important for stomach trouble.
I took stomach medicine and felt a bit better.
My friend was hospitalized for a stomach disorder.

explain: 위나 장이 오래 안 좋은 상태를 넓게 부르는 말이에요. 병명이 아니라 '위장 쪽 병'이라는 느낌이라서 일상에서 많이 써요. 병원에서는 '위염', '장염'처럼 더 정확한 이름을 말해요.
explain_en: It is a broad term for long-term stomach or bowel problems. It is not a precise diagnosis but a general 'stomach-area illness', so it is common in daily talk. Hospitals use more exact names like '위염' or '장염'.

examples.en: I ate spoiled food and got gastroenteritis.

examples.ko: 위장염 때문에 이틀 동안 죽만 먹었어요.
examples.en: Because of gastroenteritis, I ate only porridge for two days.
The doctor said it was acute gastroenteritis.
I stayed home from school until the gastroenteritis cleared up.
The child had a fever and vomited from gastroenteritis.

examples.ko: 위장염은 손을 자주 씻으면 예방할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can prevent gastroenteritis by washing your hands often.

explain: 위와 장에 염증이 생겨 배가 아프고 토하거나 설사하는 병이에요. 보통 '위장염에 걸리다'로 말해요. '위장병'은 넓은 말이고 '위장염'은 염증이 있는 병이에요.
explain_en: It is an illness where the stomach and intestines are inflamed, causing stomach pain, vomiting or diarrhea. It is usually said as '위장염에 걸리다'. '위장병' is a broad term, while '위장염' is specifically an inflammation.

examples.en: The shop owner found a counterfeit bill.
Counterfeit bills feel different when you touch them.
Banks use a machine to check for counterfeit bills.
I saw news that counterfeit bills are circulating.
I worried that the change I got might be a counterfeit bill.

examples.ko: 이 위조지폐는 진짜와 거의 똑같아 보여요.
examples.en: This counterfeit bill looks almost identical to a real one.

explain: 가짜로 만든 돈을 말해요. 일상에서는 '가짜 돈'이라고도 하지만 뉴스나 은행에서는 '위조지폐'를 써요. 주로 '위조지폐를 만들다/발견하다'로 나와요.
explain_en: It means money that was made fake. In daily talk people also say '가짜 돈', but news and banks use '위조지폐'. It mostly appears as '위조지폐를 만들다/발견하다'.

examples.en: The big dog barked threateningly, so I was scared.
His way of speaking is very threatening.

examples.ko: 위협적인 분위기 때문에 아무도 말하지 못했어요.
examples.en: Because of the menacing atmosphere, nobody could speak.

examples.ko: 제 눈에는 그 행동이 위협적으로 보였어요.
examples.en: That behavior looked threatening to me.
A threatening opponent has appeared for our team.
The typhoon came close enough to be menacing.

explain: '위협적인 분위기', '위협적으로 보이다'처럼 상대를 불안하고 무섭게 만드는 느낌을 말할 때 써요. 사람의 행동뿐 아니라 경쟁 상대나 자연 현상에도 쓸 수 있어요. 비슷한 '무서운'보다 해를 줄 것 같다는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is used in phrases like '위협적인 분위기' or '위협적으로 보이다' for something that makes you feel anxious or afraid. It applies to people's behavior but also to rivals or natural events. Compared with '무서운', it feels more like something might do harm.

examples.en: Slowly bend your upper body forward.

examples.ko: 윗몸 일으키기를 매일 오십 번 해요.
examples.en: I do fifty sit-ups every day.
My upper body was stiff, so I stretched.
The child is leaning their upper body out the window.
Relax your upper body when you exercise.
Swimming makes your upper body strong.

explain: 허리 위쪽 몸을 말해요. 가장 자주 만나는 곳은 체육 시간의 '윗몸 일으키기'예요. 반대로 허리 아래는 '아랫몸'이라고 하지만 일상에서는 '상체/하체'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means the part of the body above the waist. The place you most often meet it is '윗몸 일으키기' (sit-ups) in P.E. The opposite is '아랫몸', but in daily life '상체/하체' are used more.

examples.en: When an elder arrives, you should give up the seat of honor.
We seated grandfather in the seat of honor at the restaurant.
The seat of honor is the one farther from the door.
It feels awkward, so I don't want to sit in the seat of honor.

examples.ko: 윗자리가 비어 있으면 어른이 아직 안 오신 거예요.
examples.en: If the seat of honor is empty, the elder hasn't arrived yet.
At company dinners, we decide the senior seats first and sit down.

explain: 모임이나 식사에서 나이나 직위가 높은 사람이 앉는 자리예요. 보통 방 안쪽이나 문에서 먼 쪽을 말하지만 장소마다 달라요. 반대말은 '아랫자리'이고, 어른에게는 '윗자리에 앉으세요'처럼 높임말로 안내해요.
explain_en: It is the seat where the older or higher-ranking person sits at a gathering or meal. It is often the inner side or the side far from the door, but it varies by place. The opposite is '아랫자리', and to an elder you say it politely, like '윗자리에 앉으세요'.

examples.en: A mosquito is buzzing around my ear.
The fridge hums all night.
Bees are gathered buzzing in the flower field.
The fan whirs around and it's noisy.

examples.ko: 드론이 머리 위에서 윙윙 날고 있어요.
examples.en: A drone is whizzing above my head.

examples.ko: 귀에서 윙윙 소리가 나서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My ears were ringing, so I went to the hospital.

explain: 벌, 모기, 기계가 빠르게 돌 때 나는 낮고 계속되는 소리예요. 보통 '윙윙 소리가 나다', '윙윙거리다'로 써요. 귀에서 나는 소리에도 쓰는데, 몸이 안 좋을 때 쓰는 말이니 병원 이야기와 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a low, continuous sound made by bees, mosquitoes or fast-spinning machines. It is used as '윙윙 소리가 나다' or '윙윙거리다'. It also describes ringing in the ears, so it often shows up in talk about health.

examples.ko: 빨간 코트를 입은 사람이 사람들 사이에서 유난히 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: The person in the red coat stood out unusually among the crowd.

examples.ko: 오늘따라 보름달이 유난히 크고 밝아서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The full moon was especially big and bright tonight, so I took a photo.
This winter feels especially long.

examples.ko: 동생은 어릴 때부터 겁이 유난히 많았어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has been especially timid since childhood.

examples.ko: 그는 유난한 성격이라 같이 있으면 피곤해요.
examples.en: He has such a fussy personality that it is tiring to be with him.

examples.ko: 유난한 더위 때문에 에어컨을 하루 종일 켰어요.
examples.en: Because of the exceptional heat, I ran the air conditioner all day.

explain: 실제로는 '유난히'의 형태로 가장 많이 쓰이고, '유난히 크다/예쁘다'처럼 다른 것보다 눈에 띄게 다르다는 느낌을 줘요. '유난하다' 자체는 '유난한 날씨'처럼 쓸 수 있지만 '유난히'보다 드물어요. 사람에게 '유난이다/유난 떨다'라고 하면 지나치게 호들갑스럽다는 말이 돼요.
explain_en: In practice it appears most often as '유난히', as in '유난히 크다/예쁘다', meaning noticeably different from the rest. The adjective itself, as in '유난한 날씨', is possible but rarer than '유난히'. Saying '유난이다/유난 떨다' about a person means they make a bigger fuss than necessary.

examples.en: I was unusually tired today, so I went to bed early.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 유달리 책 읽기를 좋아해요.
examples.en: That child especially loves reading books.
The autumn leaves are exceptionally pretty this fall.
Father cherished our youngest in a special way.
Today the wind is blowing exceptionally hard.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 유달리 손님이 많이 와요.
examples.en: That shop gets an unusually large number of customers.

explain: '유난히'와 거의 비슷하게 다른 것보다 특별히 더하다는 뜻으로 써요. 말할 때는 '유난히'가 더 자주 들리고, '유달리'는 글이나 이야기체에서 조금 더 많이 보여요. 뒤에 '크다, 피곤하다, 좋아하다'처럼 정도를 나타내는 말이 자주 와요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '유난히', meaning especially more than others. In speech '유난히' is heard more, while '유달리' shows up a bit more in writing and storytelling. It is often followed by words of degree like '크다', '피곤하다' or '좋아하다'.

examples.ko: 둘째 날에는 배를 타고 바다를 유람했어요.
examples.en: On the second day we toured the sea by boat.

examples.ko: 밤에 한강을 유람하는 배를 타려고 해요.
examples.en: I'm planning to ride a boat that tours the Han River at night.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 배를 타고 강을 유람했대요.
examples.en: I heard people in the old days toured the river by boat.
I want to tour Jeju Island with my parents.

examples.ko: 이번 휴가에는 남해안을 천천히 유람할 거예요.
examples.en: This vacation I will leisurely tour the south coast.

examples.ko: 유람하는 기분으로 걸었더니 하나도 안 힘들었어요.
examples.en: I walked as if on a leisure tour, so it wasn't tiring at all.

explain: 여기저기 경치를 즐기며 돌아다닌다는 느낌이라 조금 옛스럽고 글 같은 말이에요. 일상에서는 '여행하다', '관광하다', '구경하다'를 더 많이 써요. 대신 '유람선'이라는 말은 지금도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of wandering and enjoying scenery, and it sounds a little old-fashioned and bookish. In daily life '여행하다', '관광하다' or '구경하다' are used more. The word '유람선' (cruise boat), however, is still very common.

examples.en: We learned rational and irrational numbers in math class.

examples.ko: 분수로 나타낼 수 있는 수는 유리수예요.
examples.en: A number that can be written as a fraction is a rational number.
All integers are included among the rational numbers.
The answer to this problem is not a rational number.
Adding rational numbers is the same as calculating with fractions.

examples.ko: 선생님이 칠판에 유리수를 몇 개 적으셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher wrote a few rational numbers on the board.

explain: 수학 시간에 나오는 말로, 짝이 되는 말은 '무리수'예요. '유리수'와 '무리수'를 함께 묻는 문제가 많아요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 수업과 교재에서 만나요.
explain_en: This is a math-class word, and its counterpart is '무리수' (irrational number). Questions often ask about both together. It is rarely used in daily talk and mostly appears in lessons and textbooks.

examples.en: Our teacher's classes are always humorous.

examples.ko: 유머러스한 사람과 있으면 시간이 빨리 가요.
examples.en: Time goes by fast when I'm with a humorous person.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 인터뷰도 유머러스하게 해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That actor does his interviews humorously too, so he is popular.
The content was funny, so I laughed while reading the book.

examples.ko: 저는 유머러스하지 않아서 농담을 잘 못해요.
examples.en: I'm not humorous, so I'm bad at making jokes.
If you start a presentation humorously, the mood gets better.

explain: 사람의 말이나 글, 분위기가 웃음을 주는 좋은 느낌일 때 써요. 그냥 '웃기다'는 상황이 우스울 때도 쓰지만, '유머러스하다'는 재치 있고 센스 있다는 칭찬에 가까워요. 외래어에서 온 말이라 '유머 감각이 있다'로 바꿔 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone's words, writing or mood is pleasantly funny. '웃기다' can describe any funny situation, while '유머러스하다' is closer to praising someone as witty. It comes from a loanword, and people also say '유머 감각이 있다' instead.

examples.ko: 이 역은 사람이 많아도 유별나게 시끄럽지는 않아요.
examples.en: Even with many people, this station isn't especially noisy.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 입맛이 유별나서 음식 고르기가 어려워요.
examples.en: My child has peculiar tastes, so choosing food is hard.
That friend is fussy about cleaning.
The cold was exceptionally harsh this winter.
If you act peculiarly, people stare at you.

examples.ko: 그 집 강아지는 주인을 유별나게 따라요.
examples.en: That family's puppy follows its owner in a special way.

explain: 남들과 다르게 눈에 띄거나 유난히 까다로울 때 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 '지나치게 별나다'는 약간 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '특별하다'는 좋은 뜻이 많지만 '유별나다'는 좋고 나쁨보다 '평범하지 않다'는 쪽에 가까워요.
explain_en: It is used when something stands out as different, or when someone is unusually picky. About a person it can sound slightly negative, like 'overly peculiar'. '특별하다' is often positive, whereas '유별나다' leans toward 'not ordinary' rather than good or bad.

examples.en: There are many similarities between the two languages.
I analyzed the similarity between the two incidents.

examples.ko: 이 이야기와 옛날이야기의 유사성이 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The similarity between this story and the old tale is noticeable.

examples.ko: 유사성만으로는 같은 사람이라고 말할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't say it's the same person from similarity alone.

examples.ko: 선생님이 두 그림의 유사성에 대해 물으셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher asked about the similarity between the two pictures.
After comparing them, there was almost no similarity.

explain: 둘 이상을 비교할 때 비슷한 점이 있다는 말이에요. 발표나 보고서에서 '유사성이 있다/높다'로 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '비슷한 점'이라고 쉽게 말하고, 반대말은 '차이점'이에요.
explain_en: It refers to the fact that things being compared have something in common. It is often used in presentations and reports as '유사성이 있다/높다'. In daily talk people simply say '비슷한 점', and the opposite is '차이점'.

examples.en: Be careful of look-alike products online.
There are too many knockoffs of this bag.
The box says 'Beware of imitations'.

examples.ko: 싼 유사품을 샀다가 금방 고장 났어요.
examples.en: I bought a cheap imitation and it broke soon.
It is hard to tell the imitation from the real one.
Quality is not guaranteed for imitation products.

explain: 진짜와 비슷하게 만든 다른 회사의 물건을 말해요. 제품 포장에 '유사품 주의'라고 쓰여 있는 것을 자주 봐요. '가짜'보다 덜 직접적이지만, 진짜가 아닐 수 있다는 경고의 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means goods that look like the real thing but are made by someone else. You often see '유사품 주의' on product packaging. It is less blunt than '가짜' but still warns that it may not be genuine.

examples.en: I bought baby clothes as a gift for my nephew.

examples.ko: 백화점 삼 층에 유아복 매장이 있어요.
examples.en: The department store has a baby clothes shop on the third floor.
Soft cotton is best for toddler clothes.

examples.ko: 아이가 빨리 커서 유아복이 금방 작아졌어요.
examples.en: The child grew fast, so the toddler clothes got too small quickly.
These toddler clothes are fine in the washing machine.
Many parents buy toddler clothes secondhand.

explain: 아기와 어린 아이가 입는 옷을 모아 부르는 말이에요. 가게 이름이나 매장 안내에서 '유아복 매장'처럼 자주 보여요. 조금 더 큰 아이 옷은 '아동복'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a collective term for clothes worn by babies and young children. You often see it in shop names and store directories, like '유아복 매장'. Clothes for slightly older kids are called '아동복'.

examples.en: Try finding a synonym for this word.
In Korean, the synonym of the word for 'big' is the word for 'huge'.
The dictionary lists synonyms together.
Even synonyms differ a little in how they're used.
A question about choosing synonyms came up on the exam.

examples.ko: 이 말과 유의어 관계인 단어가 뭐예요?
examples.en: What word is a synonym of this one?

explain: 뜻이 비슷한 말을 가리켜요. 반대말은 '반의어'이고, '비슷한말'이라고 쉽게 말하기도 해요. 유의어라도 쓰는 상황이나 느낌이 다를 수 있어서 바꿔 쓸 때 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: It refers to words with similar meanings. The opposite is '반의어' (antonym), and people also say '비슷한말' in plain terms. Synonyms can differ in situation or feeling, so be careful when swapping them.

examples.en: Owning a car costs a lot in maintenance.
I moved to cut down on housing upkeep costs.
I'm looking for a car with low maintenance costs.
How much is the website's upkeep per month?
I heard they decided to close the pool because of upkeep costs.
Insurance is included in the building's maintenance costs.

explain: 물건이나 시설을 계속 쓰기 위해 드는 돈이에요. 주로 '유지비가 들다/많이 나오다/줄이다'로 써요. 차를 사거나 집을 구할 때 처음 값만큼 이 돈도 중요하다고 말해요.
explain_en: It is the money needed to keep something or some facility in use. It is commonly used as '유지비가 들다/많이 나오다/줄이다'. People say that when buying a car or home, this cost matters as much as the initial price.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 전국에 유통망을 갖고 있어요.
examples.en: This company has a distribution network across the country.

examples.ko: 유통망이 좋아서 어디서나 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: The distribution network is good, so you can buy it anywhere.
They are expanding the distribution network for the new product.

examples.ko: 작은 농가는 유통망이 약해서 판매가 어려워요.
examples.en: Small farms have weak distribution networks, so selling is hard.
Because of the distribution network, delivery is slow in the countryside.
As online distribution networks grew, stores decreased.

explain: 물건이 만든 곳에서 소비자에게 가는 길 전체를 말해요. 뉴스와 경제 기사에서 '유통망을 넓히다/확보하다'로 자주 나와요. 생활에서는 '물건이 어떻게 들어오는지'처럼 풀어서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It means the whole route goods travel from where they're made to consumers. In news and economy articles it often appears as '유통망을 넓히다/확보하다'. In daily life people may explain it as 'how goods come in'.

examples.en: In winter, epidemics like the flu go around.
When the epidemic spread, the school closed.

examples.ko: 이 지역에서는 유행병 예방 주사를 무료로 맞아요.
examples.en: In this region you can get epidemic prevention shots for free.

examples.ko: 유행병을 막으려면 손을 자주 씻어야 해요.
examples.en: To stop an epidemic, you should wash your hands often.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 유행병 때문에 많은 사람이 힘들었대요.
examples.en: I heard many people suffered because of epidemics long ago.

examples.ko: 유행병은 처음 보고된 곳에서 빨리 번져요.
examples.en: An epidemic spreads quickly from where it was first reported.

explain: 짧은 기간에 많은 사람에게 퍼지는 병을 말해요. 보통 '유행병이 돌다/퍼지다'로 써요. 더 넓게 전 세계로 퍼지는 병은 '팬데믹'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a disease that spreads to many people in a short time. It is usually used as '유행병이 돌다/퍼지다'. A disease spreading worldwide is called a '팬데믹'.

examples.en: A beehive is shaped like hexagons.
Try drawing a hexagon on the paper.
A hexagon has six angles in all.
Most snow crystals are shaped like hexagons.
This pencil is hexagonal, so it is comfortable to hold.
A soccer ball has many hexagon patterns.

explain: 변이 여섯 개인 도형으로, 수학 시간에 '삼각형, 사각형, 오각형' 다음에 나와요. 자연에서는 벌집이나 눈 결정에서 많이 볼 수 있어요. 한자어 숫자로 '육'을 쓴다는 점이 '오각형, 칠각형'과 같아요.
explain_en: It is a shape with six sides, and in math class it follows '삼각형, 사각형, 오각형'. In nature you see it in beehives and snow crystals. It uses the Sino-Korean number '육', like '오각형' and '칠각형'.

examples.en: Manual labor is physically very tiring.
My father did manual labor all his life.
You need to rest enough after manual labor.

examples.ko: 저는 사무직보다 육체노동이 더 맞는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think manual labor suits me better than office work.
We talked about the difference between manual and mental labor.
I tried a manual labor part-time job during vacation.

explain: 몸을 써서 하는 일을 말하고, 반대말은 '정신노동'이에요. 일상에서는 '몸 쓰는 일'이라고도 해요. 직업을 낮춰 보는 말로 들리지 않도록 조심해서 쓰는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It refers to work done with the body, and its opposite is '정신노동' (mental labor). In daily talk people also say '몸 쓰는 일'. Be careful to use it so it doesn't sound like looking down on a job.

examples.ko: 올해는 윤년이라서 이월이 이십구 일까지 있어요.
examples.en: This is a leap year, so February has 29 days.

examples.ko: 윤년은 사 년에 한 번 돌아와요.
examples.en: A leap year comes around once every four years.

examples.ko: 저는 윤년에 태어나서 생일이 사 년마다 있어요.
examples.en: I was born in a leap year, so my birthday comes every four years.
Do you know when the next leap year is?
In a leap year, there are 366 days.

examples.ko: 달력을 보고 이번 해가 윤년인지 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked the calendar to see whether this year is a leap year.

explain: 하루가 더 있는 해를 말해요. 반대는 평년이에요. '윤년'은 날이 더해지고 '윤달'은 달이 더해지는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a year with an extra day, and the opposite is '평년'. '윤년' adds a day, whereas '윤달' adds a month.

examples.en: This year has a leap month in the lunar calendar.

examples.ko: 윤달은 보통 삼 년에 한 번쯤 돌아와요.
examples.en: A leap month comes around about once every three years.
Grandmother said it's good to move in a leap month.
A year with a leap month has thirteen months.
The lunar calendar marks the leap month separately.

examples.ko: 윤달에는 이사를 해도 탈이 없다고 해요.
examples.en: They say it's fine to move house during a leap month.

explain: 음력에서 날짜를 맞추려고 더하는 달이에요. '윤년'과 이름이 비슷하지만 윤년은 양력의 하루, 윤달은 음력의 한 달이라 달라요. 풍습과 함께 말하는 경우가 많아서 어른들과의 대화에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a month added to the lunar calendar to keep dates aligned. The name resembles '윤년', but '윤년' adds a day to the solar calendar while '윤달' adds a month to the lunar one. It often comes up with customs, so you hear it in conversations with older people.

examples.en: On New Year's Day, we threw the yut sticks with family.

examples.ko: 윷이 한 번에 네 개 다 뒤집어졌어요.
examples.en: All four yut sticks flipped over at once.

examples.ko: 윷은 나무 막대 네 개로 만들어요.
examples.en: Yut is made of four wooden sticks.
Grandfather threw the yut sticks and got a mo.

examples.ko: 모와 윷이 나오면 한 번 더 던져요.
examples.en: If you get a mo or a yut, you throw once more.

examples.ko: 아이들이 윷 던지는 법을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: The children are learning how to throw yut.

explain: '윷'은 놀이 도구이면서 던져서 나온 결과 중 하나(도, 개, 걸, 윷, 모)이기도 해요. 놀이 전체는 '윷놀이'라고 하고 설날에 가족이 함께 많이 해요. 말할 때는 '윷을 던지다'로 써요.
explain_en: '윷' is both the game's set of sticks and one of the throw results (도, 개, 걸, 윷, 모). The whole game is called '윷놀이', and families often play it on New Year's. It is used as '윷을 던지다'.

examples.en: I mash the boiled potatoes with a fork.
Mash the banana, then mix it with milk.
I crushed the tofu by hand and put it in.

examples.ko: 마늘을 칼로 으깨면 향이 더 진해요.
examples.en: If you crush garlic with a knife, the aroma gets stronger.
The child crushed the snack and spilled it on the floor.
I made a tasty snack with mashed sweet potato.

explain: 단단하지 않은 것을 눌러서 형태가 없게 만들 때 써요. 요리에서 '감자, 바나나, 두부, 마늘'과 자주 같이 써요. '부수다'는 단단한 것이 깨질 때, '으깨다'는 부드러운 것을 눌러서 뭉갤 때라서 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when you press something soft until it loses its shape. In cooking it often goes with potatoes, bananas, tofu and garlic. '부수다' is for breaking something hard, while '으깨다' is for squashing something soft.

examples.en: The puppy growls when it sees a stranger.
I was scared to walk past the growling dog.

examples.ko: 고양이 두 마리가 서로 으르렁거리고 있어요.
examples.en: Two cats are snarling at each other.
When the lion roared, the kids were startled.
Those brothers snarl at each other whenever they meet.
If a dog growls, don't go near it.

explain: 개, 고양이, 사자 같은 동물이 화가 나서 낮고 거칠게 소리를 낼 때 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 서로 사이가 나빠서 거칠게 말하거나 싸울 듯이 대한다는 비유가 돼요. 흔히 '서로 으르렁거리다'로 써요.
explain_en: It describes animals like dogs, cats and lions making a low, rough sound when angry. About people, it figuratively means being on bad terms and speaking harshly as if ready to fight. It is commonly used as '서로 으르렁거리다'.

examples.ko: 복도 형광등이 오래돼서 밤이 되면 어둡고 으스스해요.
examples.en: The hallway lights are old, so it's dark and eerie at night.
When the cold wind blew, my body shivered.
I feel chilly, as if I'm catching a cold.

examples.ko: 으스스한 이야기를 들으니 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: After hearing a creepy story, I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 폐가 앞을 지나니 으스스했어요.
examples.en: Passing the abandoned house on a rainy day felt eerie.
I feel a chill in the mornings and evenings.

explain: 몸이 차갑거나 무서워서 소름 끼칠 때 쓰는 말이에요. 보통 '으스스 춥다/떨리다'로 쓰고, '으스스하다'로 분위기가 무서울 때도 써요. 감기 기운이 있을 때 쓰는 말로도 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It describes the feeling when you are cold or scared and get goosebumps. It is usually '으스스 춥다/떨리다', and '으스스하다' is used for a creepy atmosphere. It is also natural for the chills you get when coming down with a cold.

examples.en: Avoid secluded alleys at night.
We wandered only through secluded back alleys.

examples.ko: 공원 안쪽은 으슥해서 혼자 가기 무서워요.
examples.en: The inside of the park is secluded, so it's scary to go alone.
A strange sound came from a hidden place.
After sunset, the forest path became gloomy and secluded.

examples.ko: 으슥한 길에서는 휴대폰을 보며 걷지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't walk looking at your phone on a secluded road.

explain: 사람이 별로 없고 구석져서 조용하며 조금 무서운 곳에 써요. '으슥한 골목/길/곳'처럼 뒤에 장소가 오는 경우가 많아요. 단순히 조용한 곳을 말하는 '한적하다'와 달리 불안한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a place with few people, tucked away, quiet and a little scary. It is often followed by a place word, like '으슥한 골목/길/곳'. Unlike '한적하다', which just means quiet, it carries a feeling of unease.

examples.en: When I got praised, my shoulders rose proudly.

examples.ko: 그는 모른다는 듯 어깨를 으쓱 올렸어요.
examples.en: He shrugged his shoulders as if he didn't know.
He boasted proudly that he came first.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 옷을 입고 으쓱 거울을 봤어요.
examples.en: The child looked in the mirror proudly in new clothes.

examples.ko: 친구는 어깨를 으쓱 올리고 그냥 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend gave a shrug and just smiled.
The teacher's words made me feel proud and happy.

explain: 어깨를 한 번 올리는 모양이나, 칭찬받아 우쭐한 기분을 나타내요. 보통 '어깨를 으쓱' 형태로 자주 보여요. 어깨를 올려 '몰라요/별거 아니에요' 하는 몸짓에도, 자랑스러운 마음에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It shows a quick lift of the shoulders, or the proud feeling of being praised. It often appears as '어깨를 으쓱'. It can describe a shrug meaning 'I don't know / no big deal' or a feeling of pride.

examples.en: I feel proud hearing the compliment.

examples.ko: 아이가 상을 받고 으쓱한 얼굴로 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: The child came back with a proud face after winning a prize.
Being praised in front of friends made my shoulders lift proudly.
Wearing new shoes makes me feel proud for no reason.
He shrugged his shoulders and avoided answering.
My younger sibling got puffed up and started bragging.

explain: 칭찬이나 좋은 일 때문에 우쭐해지고 기분이 좋아질 때 많이 써요. 어깨를 한번 올리는 동작에도 쓸 수 있지만 일상에서는 '어깨가 으쓱하다'처럼 기분을 말하는 쓰임이 흔해요. 부사 '으쓱'과 짝이에요.
explain_en: It is often used when praise or good news makes you feel puffed up and happy. It can also describe lifting the shoulders, but in daily life the feeling sense, like '어깨가 으쓱하다', is common. It pairs with the adverb '으쓱'.
